solutions.explanation:
Factoring exposes the common factors that can cancel. The identity
\[
(x-r)(x-s)=x^2-(r+s)x+rs
\]
lets us factor each quadratic by matching the sum and product of \(r\) and \(s\). The expression becomes
\[
\frac{(x-1)(x-2)}{(x-2)(x-3)}
\div
\frac{(x-1)(x-4)}{(x-3)(x-4)}.
\]
The original denominators require \(x\ne2,3,4\). The fraction used as the divisor must also be nonzero, which additionally requires \(x\ne1\).

For \(x\notin\{1,2,3,4\}\), division by the second fraction is multiplication by its reciprocal:
\[
\frac{(x-1)(x-2)}{(x-2)(x-3)}
\cdot
\frac{(x-3)(x-4)}{(x-1)(x-4)}=1.
\]
All cancelled factors are nonzero on this domain. Thus the simplified value is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\text{D}\), with the original exclusions retained.
solutions.title: Factor and multiply by the reciprocal
